confidence_notes: I ran two web searches: one for the RBA exchange rate and one for Jeonju cost-of-living sites, which rely on user-submitted prices. Beer, coffee and the inexpensive meal are based on those sites, but they disagree. Cappuccino ranges from about $1.50 to $3.70 and an inexpensive meal from about $5.30 to $6. I picked values near the top of each range because of inflation and July 2026 pricing. The sites put a mid-range dinner for two at $21-28, which looks low for a three-course meal, so I set it higher. Beer is uncertain: one site says a domestic pint costs about $3.04 and another lists beer at about $4.50 a pint. I estimated cocktail and wine from general knowledge of Korean bar prices and their usual markup over beer; I did not search for them. All four accommodation figures are general estimates, not taken from any booking site. July demand around Jeonju Hanok Village could push room rates up.
comparable_city_reasoning: Jeonju is a mid-sized South Korean regional city. One site says it is cheaper than Seoul and Jeju. I scaled typical prices from other regional Korean cities such as Gwangju and Daejeon, with a small premium on rooms near the Hanok Village tourist area.
